No: the reviewer must supply or confirm the technical basis

The reviewer must supply or confirm:

  • Technique: coach-authored movement phases, cues and timing for this trick.
  • Progression: coach-authored stages with consistency gates, feature selection and facility requirements.
  • Corrections: a coach-approved correction for each common error.
  • Readiness: the prerequisites and stop criteria the coach will check in person.
  • Mistake corrections: fish whip, straight takeoff/forced whip, late recovery.

Lesson goal

Define a controlled whip, compare how two expert sources explain it, and build an error library.

What it will cover

  • A controlled whip versus an uncontrolled sideways movement
  • Compare the Söderström article with the Samson video
  • Takeoff context, controlling the shape, recovering alignment
  • Slow-motion front, side and rear examples
  • Error library: fish whip, insufficient recovery, inconsistent direction, off-axis landing

Safety

Class 2: advanced riding skills. Needs the stated prerequisites, a controlled progression, suitable terrain and coaching guidance.

Practice only on terrain your coach has chosen, within your current skill, with the right protective equipment. Completing a lesson isn’t a safety certificate and doesn’t mean a rider is ready to try anything.
